newsitem.title: JAPAN: Lease buy-back schemes may boost Japan car sales.
newsitem.headline: Lease buy-back schemes may boost Japan car sales.

text.p: Japanese car sales were down last month as a rise in the country's sales tax drove away buyers, but dealers are pinning their hopes on new leasing plans to lure them back into showrooms.

"We expect the car leasing business to boom in the future, said Shouji Hidaka, sales manager at Tokyo Nissan Motor Sales, which has started to lease cars to customers with an option to buy at the end of the contract term.
"The monthly cost of leasing a car is cheaper than through installment payments. We expect car leasing to help boost our sales," said Hidaka, whose firm is a dealer for Nissan Motor Co Ltd cars.

Dealers are hoping that potential car buyers, deterred by rising sticker prices as a result of the higher sales tax, may find leasing with an option to buy cheaper and more flexible than paying in installments which also require a large down payment.

Japan's domestic vehicle sales fell 9.4 percent in May from a year earlier to 319,940 vehicles, the Japan Automobile Dealers Association (JADA) said. Of the total, sales of imported vehicles fell a steep 27 percent in May to 22,921.
The May drop followed a decline of 12.7 percent in April.
Most Japanese consumers buy cars through installment payments or pay in full. But car leasing is beginning to catch on, particularly with younger consumers.

Mitsuo Auto Lease, the car leasing unit of Mitsui & Co Ltd , has started a guaranteed buy-back programme for its StarCraft luxury minivan, which is based on General Motors Corp's Astro model and sold by Mitsui.

Customers who choose the two-year lease option can buy the vehicle at 55 percent of the retail price, or at 45 percent under the three-year lease or 35 percent under the four-year lease, a Mitsui spokesman said.
Under a guaranteed buy-back programme, a consumer essentially rents a car from car dealers.
After the first few years, customers can simply hand the car back to the dealer, purchase it at the pre-arranged and guaranteed buy-back price or seek to refinance the car.
"Guaranteed buy-back programmes offered by car dealers will make it easy to buy expensive cars," said Nobuaki Yanachi, a Kankaku Research senior analyst.

Rover Japan, the Japanese unit of Rover Group, started its own leasing system called "Smart Ownership", a guaranteed buy-back programme, in September 1996. Rover is the British unit of Bayerische Motoren-Werke AG.
Rover Japan has boosted its domestic sales since October last year, posting a steep 91.1 percent year-on-year gain in sales for January and 90.4 percent for February.
"The success of Rover's sales method started a wave of similar guaranteed buy-back programmes by imported car dealers," the Mitsui spokesman said.
"The cheaper monthly payments have attracted customers, especially young people," a Rover Japan spokeswoman said.
Ford Sales Japan Ltd, the Japanese sales unit of Ford Motor Co, started its own buy-back programme called the "Red Carpet Program" on May 31.
Other car dealers, imported car dealers in particular, are likely to follow suit.
